cards.title: Isotropic connected-correlation kernel
cards.numerical_form: finite transfer correlations and an exact reflection-plus-spin-flip symmetry check

checks.reason: The complete correlation kernel is printed in the final isotropic paragraph.

The printed leading kernel has an O(1/n) mirror-symmetry violation while the exact finite NESS respects the symmetry to 7.2e-14. The gate remains closed until fresh review adjudicates the discrepancy.

open_questions: Does the printed connected-correlation kernel contain a variable or sign transcription error?

cards.title: Finite MPO theorem and commutator identity
cards.latex: R=S_n S_n^dagger; [H,S_n]=-i epsilon (sigma^z tensor S_(n-1)-S_(n-1) tensor sigma^z)
derived_from: printed auxiliary matrices, boundary algebra and Cholesky construction
cards.numerical_form: explicit small-chain physical MPO matrices and unrelated dense Liouvillian fixed points

checks.reason: The theorem, auxiliary matrices and boundary commutator are printed in Eqs. (4)-(10).
Explicit S_n S_n^dagger agrees entry by entry with the dense Liouvillian NESS for n=2,3,4 over the declared anisotropy/coupling grid.
The finite commutator identity and full Lindblad residual pass at machine precision.

cards.title: Finite-size structural corollaries
cards.role: T008-T011 Cholesky, truncation, polynomial and observable claims
cards.latex: S_n upper triangular with diag(S_n)=1; d=1+floor(n/2); deg_epsilon(R)=2n-2
derived_from: explicit physical MPO contraction and finite auxiliary return paths
cards.numerical_form: small-chain matrix identities plus epsilon-squared polynomial interpolation

checks.reason: Corollaries (ii)-(v) explicitly state triangularity, full rank, the finite auxiliary cutoff and polynomial degree.
Upper triangularity, unit diagonal, positive full rank and exact minimal-dimension truncation pass for all declared small chains.
Degree 2n-2 fits have residual below 1e-11, nonzero leading coefficients and fail when forced two degrees lower.
The paper states that a local observable can be evaluated with O(n^2) operations.
The deterministic contraction operation-count exponent is within 0.05 of two.

cards.title: Root-of-unity cutoff index and parity
cards.latex: lambda=pi l/m; printed: a_m^+=0 (odd m) or a_m^-=0 (even m), dim H=m+1; Eq. (7): a_{m-1}^-=0 (odd m) or a_{m-1}^+=0 (even m), dim H=m

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf p. 4, root-of-unity paragraph before Eq. (19)

derived_from: direct substitution into the printed Eq. (7) amplitudes
cards.numerical_form: complete Eq. (7) amplitudes at r=m and r=m-1 for m=3..8

checks.reason: The cutoff index, plus/minus assignment and m+1-dimensional space are printed explicitly.

With the nonsingular tau prescription, the paper-named r=m component is nonzero, whereas the opposite hopping at r=m-1 vanishes exactly and yields the m-state space used by the printed m=3 example; the gate remains closed until fresh review.

open_questions: Does a fresh derivation confirm that the root-of-unity prose shifts the cutoff index by one and consequently misstates both parity and auxiliary dimension?
